text:
alex: Heads-up — onboarding mistral-7b-v2 for hosted route /models/mistral-7b-v2. Seeing intermittent OOMs when batch >= 4 and max_new_tokens >= 512. Happens ~mid-latency bursts, not constant. Logs show cudamalloc failures and then retries. Suspect memory fragmentation due to rapid varying seq lengths + KV cache growth.

riley: Ugh. Any relation to quant or int8 path? or only fp16? :thinking:

alex: We're running fp16 for now. No quant yet. Also seen higher peak GPU memory when many short requests pile up. Sequence length distribution is bimodal (40 tokens and 900 tokens).

sam: Can you paste the serve config for that route? may be default batching/timeouts too aggressive.

alex: Pasting simplified route profile and recent log snippet:

```json
{
  "route": "/models/mistral-7b-v2",
  "defaults": {
    "batch_size": 8,
    "max_new_tokens": 1024,
    "prefetch_kv": true,
    "continuous_batching": true,
    "batch_timeout_ms": 50
  }
}
```

```
[2026-03-10T14:22:13Z] ERROR serve: cudamalloc failed: out of memory (requested 142MB)
[2026-03-10T14:22:13Z] WARN serve: attempt fallback variant: mistral-7b-v2-quantized not available
[2026-03-10T14:22:13Z] INFO serve: reclaiming cache blocks, freed 64MB
```

morgan: My 2c: big max_new_tokens + large batch + bimodal seq lengths = worst fragmentation pattern. Try reducing defaults and use a separate low-latency small-batch route for short requests. Also consider KV-cache pinning policy so long contexts don't hold onto fragments.

riley: Agreed. Propose: default max_new_tokens -> 256, default batch_size -> 2, enable per-request "kv_evict_threshold": 0.7, and set continuous_batching.batch_timeout_ms -> 15. That reduces window where many short+long get coalesced.

sam: Also add an allocator tweak — set environment var MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=131072 and enable CUDA context reuse. For pytorch builds we sometimes call torch.cuda.empty_cache() in the worker loop after big requests; it helps reclaim tiny slabs. Might add a small post-request defrag hook.

alex: Can someone write the exact change we want in the model profile? I'll roll it to canary.

riley: Suggested profile diff (apply to model catalog):

```diff
- "defaults": {"batch_size": 8, "max_new_tokens": 1024, "batch_timeout_ms": 50}
+ "defaults": {"batch_size": 2, "max_new_tokens": 256, "batch_timeout_ms": 15, "kv_evict_threshold": 0.7}
```

morgan: Add a special route for long-form workloads: /models/mistral-7b-v2-long with batch_size 1, prefetch_kv: false, reserve_block: true. That way clients doing long generations get isolated capacity.

ops-bot: CI check — deploying canary with new profile to dev cluster now. Link: https://ci.redwood/internal/ci/9872 :rocket:

alex: After canary deploy, two quick tests: (1) synthetic bimodal replay for 10k reqs, (2) real traffic shadowed for 30m. If OOM rate drops to <0.01% we're good.

sam: If we still see fragmentation, next step is to enable a periodic GC pass in the runtime that merges free blocks (costly but helps long-lived hosts). Also consider quantizing to int4 which often reduces peak mem but changes kernel scheduling — test on a small canary.

riley: Will update the model catalog PR and add notes in the onboarding checklist about: "set conservative defaults for max_new_tokens and batch_size; create long-form isolated route; consider allocator/env tweaks; run bimodal replay test".

alex: Thanks — I'll watch the canary. If we pass, we'll roll to staging tomorrow and communicate to CS about default max_new_tokens change so they can adjust experiments. :white_check_mark:
